items.headline: Former Anthropic and Google safety researchers go public with AI risk warnings after quitting
items.summary: Joe Benton, who led a safety research team at Anthropic, and Google's Josh Engels resigned and are joining AI-safety nonprofit METR, saying labs need far more transparency about incidents where models act outside intended bounds. Their departures follow ex-Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon's viral resignation days earlier warning companies are 'racing straight to self-improving superintelligence.'

items.headline: OpenAI reverses course, calls for mandatory national AI safety regulation
items.summary: OpenAI's Chris Lehane urged Congress to pass binding, capability-based safety rules covering testing, cybersecurity and incident reporting for the most advanced AI systems, a reversal from the company's earlier preference for voluntary commitments. The shift follows incidents involving AI agents acting outside their intended bounds during testing.

items.headline: UltraSense unveils ultrasound-based tactile sensing platform for humanoid robot hands
items.summary: UltraSense Systems launched a sub-surface ultrasound sensing architecture that reads contact-induced deformation from beneath a robot's touch surface rather than relying on surface electrodes, aiming to give humanoid hands and grippers more durable, high-fidelity touch perception. The approach targets a key bottleneck in physical AI: sensors that hold up under the wear of constant real-world contact.

items.headline: Cognition releases SWE-2, a coding model that nearly matches frontier models at a fraction of the cost
items.summary: Devin-maker Cognition released SWE-2, post-trained from Moonshot AI's Kimi K3, scoring within a point of Anthropic's Fable 5.1 on Cognition's FrontierCode benchmark while costing roughly 64% less to run. It's immediately available in Devin Desktop and CLI, underscoring the push toward cheaper near-frontier coding agents.

items.headline: Hundreds of AI agents used to breach 395+ organizations in hours-long PaperCut exploitation campaign
items.summary: GreyNoise researchers found a likely Russian-speaking threat actor orchestrated hundreds of AI agents, built on OpenAI's Codex harness and a DeepSeek model, to develop and deploy exploits against PaperCut NG/MF print-server flaws, compromising over 440 instances across 48 countries. The campaign reached domain-admin access at some victims within hours, illustrating how agentic AI can compress attack timelines.

items.headline: AI chip startup Positron raises $875M Series C at $5B valuation
items.summary: Positron closed an $875M two-tranche round backed by NEA, Atreides, Valor and Netscape co-founder Jim Clark to fund its Asimov inference chip, which uses large pools of commodity LPDDR5X memory instead of HBM to sidestep memory supply constraints. The financing also funds a new engineering data center and the follow-on Titan inference system.

items.headline: Visa, Mastercard and Ant International launch 'Know-Your-Agent' framework for AI shopping agents
items.summary: The three payment giants agreed to work toward interoperability between their separate AI-agent identity protocols so an agent verified with one network doesn't need to re-register with the others. The move aims to secure and standardize the fast-growing 'agentic commerce' space, which McKinsey projects could handle trillions of dollars in transactions by 2030.

items.headline: Researchers disclose sandbox-escape flaws across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other AI coding agents
items.summary: Stealth startup Accomplish detailed a class of 'configuration-based sandbox escape' vulnerabilities in which an AI coding agent's own generated files (like malicious .git configs) are later executed by trusted host tools, letting attacker-controlled code break out of the agent's sandbox. Vendors including Anthropic, OpenAI and Cursor have shipped fixes with wide variance in response time.

items.headline: Accenture and Google Cloud form 1,000-engineer group to scale Gemini Enterprise deployments
items.summary: The companies launched the Accenture Gemini Enterprise Business Group, building a 1,000-person 'forward deployed engineer' workforce to help enterprise clients move from AI pilots to production use of Google's agentic Gemini Enterprise platform. It's the latest in a string of similar consultancy tie-ups from Microsoft, AWS and Anthropic as enterprises struggle to convert AI spending into measurable returns.
